summary: The host side of the third APFS-root native run, finished. NAT-086 (decision 0033) showed that /chosen/ephemeral-storage=1 makes keybagd skip on the S24 and that launchd then dies at the launchd_cache_loader boot task, because the donor recipe deletes System/Library/xpc/launchd.plist on purpose. Source review of the pinned sbin/launchd (capstone disassembly, local iPhone10,3 16.5 unpack): launchd searches kern.bootargs with strstr for rd=md0 and sets a restore flag; with it a boot task runs only if PerformAlways or PerformInRestore, so only commit-boot-mode, init-with-data-volume and restore-datapartition qualify, and a missing service cache is not fatal. XNU's pexpert/gen/bootargs.c (compiled on the host with shim headers) compares whole keys, so a LAST token ' xrd=md0' leaves the kernel's rd=md1 alone while kern.bootargs (strlcpy of PE_boot_args) still contains rd=md0. build.py builds loader-diag-xnu-rm-md1 = NAT-085's image with the tag NAT087-rm1 and that token (RECOVERY 8827c97e..., Image.payload d23c71b4..., command line 236 of 255 bytes); the XNU payload is byte-for-byte NAT-085's except the command-line field. session_nat087.py is derived from session_nat085.py by 9 counted substitutions (derive87.py --check exit 0). analyze_nat087.py judges the console text after the last exec with rows R1-R9 on top of NAT-083's chain module; run over the REAL NAT-084 and NAT-086 archives it reads R5 (boot tasks not skipped), the control that separates a launchd without restore mode from one with it. 115 tests pass; mutation pass of 385 candidates: 365 killed, 15 do not parse, 5 survivors each explained in equivalent.json. Decision 0034 is written for one native run (NAT-088). Nothing here ran on the phone with this image.

acceptance.1_cmdline: test_nat087.py: KernelBootArgParser compiles XNU's real pexpert/gen/bootargs.c (pinned SHA c54f35ca...) and gets rd -> md1 and xrd -> md0 for the packaged command line (control: a last rd=md0 gives md0); KernBootargsSysctl pins kern.bootargs = PE_boot_args() in kern_sysctl.c; BuiltPayload compares Image.payload with NAT-085's byte for byte (26 differing bytes in the loader and the tag/token, the rest equal apart from the 608-byte SWEETXNU command-line field).
acceptance.2_launchd_reading: AppleLaunchd parses the Boot dictionary embedded in the pinned launchd (__TEXT,__config) and requires ALLOWED_TASKS to equal its PerformAlways/PerformInRestore set, and the strstr import and the rd=md0 string to be present. This is source review; whether launchd enters restore mode on the phone is the question of NAT-088.
acceptance.3_driver_analyser_decision: derive87.py --check exit 0 (9 substitutions); analyser rows R1-R9 over hand-written variants and the real NAT-084/NAT-086 archives (both R5); mutation pass; decision 0034 with hashes; driver preflight 'ready-read-only-registry-closed'.

findings: The first mutation pass (385 candidates) left 25 + 6 survivors. They exposed weaknesses of the first test set, none a defect of the code under test: the bounds test used the module's own constants (so changing a constant could not fail it); the stop-sign test of decide_restore was conditional (`if s['row'] == 4`) and could pass without checking anything; the text-level tests never put the kernel marker or the restore line at offset 0; the reason strings were only checked with assertIn. Eleven tests (class Boundaries and two in BuildWrapper) were added; the second full pass left 5 survivors, all explained.
decide_restore's `no $ exec` branch is unreachable through analyze() (chain row 1 needs the exec line); it is tested by calling decide_restore with a hand-built kernel reading.
NAT-087 depends on NAT-085, not on NAT-086: NAT-086's outcome is fail and it stays in_progress, so it can never be a satisfied dependency.

build.py line 42 (`b83 = b85.b83`) is a dead alias. It is left in place because build.json of the built image records the SHA-256 of build.py (nat087_sources); changing the file would make that record stale without changing the image.
established: The image, its package and its command line exist with the recorded sizes and hashes; the packaged line is NAT-085's with the tag NAT087-rm1 and ' xrd=md0' last, 236 bytes.
XNU's real boot-arg parser, compiled on the host, returns rd=md1 and xrd=md0 for it; the kern.bootargs sysctl returns the same string (source review).
Apple's launchd of the local unpack contains the strstr import, the rd=md0 string and a Boot dictionary whose PerformAlways/PerformInRestore tasks are exactly the analyser's allowed list.
The driver, the analyser and the build wrapper behave as written; 365 of 385 mutants killed, 15 unparsable, 5 equivalent with reasons.
